During a comprehensive survey of the Javan ilisha (Ilisha pristigastroides) population in the Citarum River estuary, field biologists assessed the reproductive biology of this commercially important clupeid. At a stable water temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C], a total of 200 sexually mature individuals were collected during the peak spawning season. Histological examination of ovarian tissue revealed a gonadosomatic index (GSI) of 11% [GSI = 11%] at a water temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. The sampled individuals exhibited a distinct size-related trend in maturation status, with the smallest gravid female captured measuring 19 centimeters [Lp = 19 centimeters] standard length, which was subsequently considered the standard length at puberty for this population. This size threshold marks the point at which half of the females showed signs of active vitellogenesis and gonadal recrudescence, providing a critical benchmark for fisheries management and the establishment of minimum capture size regulations.

Eggs spawned in the laboratory by gravid females of Ilisha pristigastroides were characterized by a notably small dry weight at birth. Individual fertilized ova, measured immediately after fertilization and prior to water hardening, had a mean dry weight of 0.0065 grams [Wwb = 0.0065 grams], a value derived from the measured egg diameter of 2.32 millimeters and the standard geometric relationship for spherical eggs. This minute dry mass is reflective of the low yolk content typical of pelagic spawning clupeids, which produce numerous small, buoyant eggs that undergo rapid embryonic development in warm surface waters. The incubation period was remarkably brief, with the majority of eggs hatching within 6 days [ab = 6 days] after fertilization when maintained at a constant temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. The newly emerged yolk-sac larvae, measuring approximately 3.2 millimeters in total length, were entirely reliant on their endogenous yolk reserves, initiating the lecithotrophic larval phase immediately after chorion rupture.

Growth trajectory modeling based on extensive field tagging data and otolith microstructure analysis indicated that Ilisha pristigastroides reaches a maximum lifespan of approximately 3 years [am = approximately 3 years] under natural conditions, a relatively short duration typical of many small-bodied, fast-growing tro at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]pical clupeids. This longevity estimate was derived from the analysis of daily growth increments observed in sagittal otoliths taken from individuals collected across multiple seasons at a water temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. In conjunction with this life span, the ultimate standard length recorded for the largest specimen in our survey was 30 centimeters [Li = 30 centimeters], representing the asymptotic size that individuals approach after several years of growth. This length corresponds to a total wet weight of approximately 458 grams [Wwi = approximately 458 grams] for a fully grown adult, as estimated using a length-weight regression developed specifically for this species based on a sample of 350 individuals. This value suggests a moderately robust body form for a fish of this size class.

Reproductive output exhibited a clear ontogenetic shift, with puberty marking the onset of significant gamete production. The wet weight at puberty was estimated to be 114 grams [Wwp = 114 grams], a mass that corresponds closely to the 19 centimeters standard length threshold observed earlier, confirming the allometric consistency of the maturation schedule. This relatively low body mass at first reproduction highlights a life-history strategy that prioritizes early breeding over extended somatic growth, an adaptation commonly observed in short-lived fish inhabiting unpredictable tropical estuaries. Gravid females were observed to spawn multiple batches over the breeding season, with batch fecundity correlating strongly with body size. A typical batch from a female weighing 114 grams [Wwp = 114 grams] contained approximately 8500 to 12000 oocytes, indicating that the transition from immature juvenile to spawning adult involves a substantial increase in reproductive tissue mass and the activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

Comparative analysis with the congeneric species Ilisha elongata revealed several distinct life-history traits in Ilisha pristigastroides that are likely linked to its estuarine habitat preference. A maximum lifespan of 1095 days [am = 1095 days] at 27 °C [T = 27 °C] has been recorded for the Javan ilisha, a longevity that is matched by Ilisha elongata despite the latter attaining a larger adult body size. The Javan ilisha matures at a smaller size and lower body mass, a pattern consistent with its shallower, more turbid environment. The egg diameter of 2.32 millimeters produces a dry weight at birth of 0.0065 grams [Wwb = 0.0065 grams], which is notably smaller than the eggs of Ilisha elongata, likely facilitating the development of a larger yolk-sac larva that emerges after a 6-day incubation period (6 days) [ab = 6 days] at 27 °C [T = 27 °C]. The gonadosomatic index was 11% [GSI = 11%] at a temperature of 27 °C [T = 27 °C].
